analysis.title: Moderation. Deceleration. Contraction.
key_insights: The note argues the best of the 2026 macro backdrop may be behind us. Growth expectations are being marked down, financial conditions no longer boost US GDP growth, and earnings momentum is losing breadth.

Early Q3 earnings show fewer big beats. With 10% of S&P 500 companies reported, 53% beat consensus EPS by more than one standard deviation of analyst estimates, against a 64% average over the past four quarters (FactSet).
FactSet data shows earnings revision breadth has declined over the last several weeks.
Goldman Sachs says its 2027 S&P 500 EPS forecast is 7% below bottom-up consensus. It implies the trend of large upward estimate revisions is likely behind us and that EPS growth decelerates in 2027.
Earnings growth is concentrated in AI. Morgan Stanley puts non-AI S&P 500 EPS growth at 4% next year, with AI names driving 78% of 2027 earnings growth.
BofA describes a large transfer of free cash flow from hyperscalers to semiconductor companies as a result of the AI capex boom.

Apollo's SHOK scenario models an AI reset: global credit spreads 10-30 bps wider, US investment down 1-4% and South Korean exports down 1-3%, with shocks phased in from 4Q26 and tapering through 4Q27.
Duality Research notes the S&P 500 P/E has fallen from 23.2x a year ago to 18.7x, roughly a 20% de-rating.
Bilello data cited in the note shows global inflation rates are rising.
earnings_insights: Q3 2026 season, early read (FactSet): with 10% of S&P 500 companies having reported, 53% beat consensus EPS by more than one standard deviation of analyst estimates, versus a 64% average over the past four quarters. These are reported actuals against consensus.
Goldman Sachs forecast: 2027 S&P 500 EPS estimate is 7% below the bottom-up consensus forecast.
Morgan Stanley estimate: non-AI S&P 500 EPS growth of 4% in 2027, with AI names accounting for 78% of 2027 EPS growth.
risk_factors: Earnings growth depends on one theme (AI), so a wobble there hits almost all incremental S&P 500 EPS growth.
An AI reset scenario (Apollo SHOK model) with wider credit spreads, lower US investment and lower South Korean exports.
Fading financial-conditions tailwind to US GDP growth.
Narrowing revision breadth and fewer large EPS beats.

tension_points.bull_case: AI names drive 78% of 2027 S&P 500 earnings growth (Morgan Stanley), and hyperscaler capex is transferring large free cash flow to semiconductor companies (BofA).
tension_points.bear_case: Non-AI S&P 500 EPS grows only 4% next year, so any wobble in the AI theme removes most incremental growth. Apollo's SHOK scenario models wider credit spreads and lower US investment.

theme_stances.key_argument: Growth expectations are marked down, financial conditions no longer help GDP, and earnings breadth is narrowing.
theme_stances.evidence: Things aren't necessarily getting bad, but they are incrementally getting less good.

theme_stances.key_argument: Almost all incremental S&P 500 EPS growth comes from one theme, so a stumble in AI would matter for the whole index.
